analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md (documentation). The sole changed range is head lines ~1030-1046, a new paragraph describing a PromptTokenCache in LocalTokenizerBridge, ChatTemplateLoopRewrites, and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 kill switch. The supplied units (head lines 1218-2021) are unchanged surrounding text, so I examined them for context but they contain no changed behavior. No code, configuration, or control was modified, so no security regression is evidenced.

The documented behavior raises integration questions for a code review pass, which cannot be answered from this docs-only diff. It describes a new cross-request token-ID reuse cache keyed by prefix-cache scope. Relevant threats are T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and TTFT timing oracle, SEC-035) and A-001 (prompt confidentiality). The doc states reuse never crosses a cache scope, but the actual code (PromptTokenCache.swift) is not supplied. A reviewer should verify the following:
- The scope key is the coordinator-authored cacheSalt.
- The cache is not persisted to disk.
- Cached pieces are bounded in memory and cleared on unload.
- The 4-core parallel encoding has no data race across scopes.
- Same-account timing differences from token reuse are within the accepted SEC-035 risk.
- The sampled background comparison fails closed.

The threat model's T-041 does not yet mention this in-memory prompt-token cache. A threat-model update may be warranted once the code is reviewed. I cannot confirm any of this from the supplied evidence, so I recorded it as an unverified contract rather than a finding.
